title: Unlock Hidden Value in Commercial Real Estate with Data Insights
excerpt: Discover how understanding your systems can unlock hidden value in commercial real estate. Learn the importance of data ownership and the Five Cs framework.
content:
In the ever-evolving landscape of commercial real estate, the adage “If you don't own your data & digital infrastructure, your vendors do” rings truer than ever. As we embark on this insightful journey through the latest episode of the Peak Property Performance® Podcast, we're diving into the core insight of 'Clarify'—the first step in the PPP 5C™ framework. This episode sets the stage for property owners to unlock hidden value by understanding their systems, revealing overlooked assets, and realizing the untapped potential of their building’s data.

Understanding the Five Cs Framework

The journey to Peak Property Performance® begins with understanding the Five Cs framework: Clarify, Connect, Collect, Coordinate, and Control. Today, we focus on 'Clarify', a step that demands you know exactly what systems you own, where you might be leaking value, and what your data is worth. Recognizing these factors can lead to significant savings and open up new revenue streams.

During the podcast, Bill Douglas emphasized the importance of this step:

"Know what you own, where you're leaking value, and what your data is really worth."
This foundational understanding sets the stage for the subsequent steps in the framework, effectively transforming your data and digital infrastructure from a cost center into a strategic asset.

Clarifying Ownership and Control of Data

One of the critical insights from the episode is the question of ownership and control over your building’s digital infrastructure. Bill reminded us that many commercial real estate owners unknowingly allow vendors to control their networks and systems, potentially losing out on valuable data. He stated,

"Who owns and controls your digital infrastructure? By data, we're not talking about user data, but the data generated by your building and the systems in your building."
This data, when properly harnessed, can be monetized and used to improve operational efficiency.

Imagine standing in the lobby of your building, surrounded by systems that control lighting, HVAC, and more. Each of these systems generates data, yet many building owners are unaware of its existence. Understanding what you own and control is the first step towards leveraging this data effectively.

The Role of Data in Modern CRE Systems

In today’s digital age, the systems within your building have become increasingly sophisticated, often producing modular and granular data. Drew Hall pointed out that even decisions as simple as when to turn the air conditioner on or off are backed by data. He explained, "Imagine the decisions being made in real-time in every system throughout that campus, and imagine that you have the ability to know why that decision was just made."

This level of insight allows property owners to optimize their operations, reduce costs, and enhance tenant satisfaction. However, this potential can only be unlocked if you begin with clarity. Knowing which systems generate data, and ensuring that data is accessible, is crucial for making informed decisions.

Real World Example: Finding Hidden Value

Inquisitiveness can lead to substantial savings. During the podcast, Drew recounted a story about a building engineer who discovered a forgotten lighting control system. This system, never before enabled, saved the building $56,000 in energy expenses in its first year of operation.

"It was a system that was hanging on a wall and never turned on because it was never documented, never managed, never monitored, never connected. And there was no data,"
Drew shared.

This example highlights the importance of performing a thorough review of your digital infrastructure. The savings from uncovering this single overlooked system far outweighed the cost of the review. Such discoveries are not uncommon and emphasize the importance of being inquisitive about your building’s systems.

Inquisitive Approach to System Optimization

Being inquisitive is a critical mindset for property owners seeking to optimize their systems. Bill and Drew encouraged listeners to question assumptions and explore possibilities. Drew highlighted that the lighting system, once connected and analyzed, provided insights beyond mere energy savings. It allowed for adjustments based on occupancy patterns and even facilitated the monetization of common areas.

This example underscores the value of curiosity and a willingness to explore the systems within your building. By asking questions like "What is that?" and "Can we find out more?", you open the door to uncovering hidden value and enhancing the overall performance of your property.

Preparing for the Next C: Connect

As we wrap up our discussion on 'Clarify', it’s essential to look ahead to the next step in the PPP 5C™ framework: Connect. In the upcoming episode, we will explore how connecting your systems and networks can further enhance the value derived from your digital infrastructure. The lighting system example serves as a perfect segue, as it needed to be integrated into the building’s network to maximize its potential.

Stay tuned for the next episode, where we’ll delve deeper into the importance of connectivity and how it can transform your building’s operations. Until then, we encourage you to begin your journey by clarifying your current systems and identifying opportunities for improvement.

Actionable Takeaway for CRE Owners

For commercial real estate owners, the journey to unlocking value begins with clarity. Take the time to review your building’s digital infrastructure, identify what you own, and assess the potential of your data. Remember, if you don't own your data & digital infrastructure, your vendors do. By embracing the PPP 5C™ framework, you can strategically enhance the performance of your portfolio and drive greater returns on your investments.
